page.title: How to Evaluate an AI GTM Agent Before It Acts | ProofLaunch
page.meta_description: Use a five-part evidence, authority, failure, privacy and effect test before allowing an AI GTM agent to publish, contact buyers or spend budget.
page.h1: How to evaluate an AI GTM agent before it acts
page.direct_answer: Evaluate five things separately: the source behind every claim, the named human who can release the exact artifact, the tools and side effects the agent may invoke, its recovery trace when a tool or approval fails, and observed incremental outcomes. A generated asset, passing test suite or attractive dashboard proves none of the other four.
page.approved_product_fact: ProofLaunch Cortex-X compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.

evaluation_steps.name: Trace every claim
evaluation_steps.test: Can the reviewer open the exact evidence object supporting each released clause?

evaluation_steps.name: Locate authority
evaluation_steps.test: Is one named human decision bound to the exact artifact, destination and action?

evaluation_steps.name: Bound tools and side effects
evaluation_steps.test: Can the agent publish, send, enrich, spend or mutate strategy outside its declared contract?

evaluation_steps.name: Force failure
evaluation_steps.test: Does one tool failure and one approval denial produce a located recovery trace without escaping policy?
evaluation_steps.failure: silent retry, fabricated success or operator rescue

evaluation_steps.name: Separate preparation from effect
evaluation_steps.test: Are preference, reach, conversion, revenue and incrementality kept null until genuinely observed?
evaluation_steps.failure: mechanical readiness promoted into market success

page.nonfit: Do not use this approach when the goal is automatic publishing, hidden sourcing, synthetic testimonials, unrestricted scraping, automatic spend or business outcomes stated before observation.

faqs.question: What is an AI GTM agent?
faqs.answer: An AI GTM agent coordinates bounded research, strategy, asset creation, review, activation preparation and learning across a go-to-market workflow. Its quality depends on evidence, authority, recovery and measurement—not the number of tools it can call.

faqs.question: How should a company evaluate an AI GTM agent?
faqs.answer: Use the same rights-cleared brief for every candidate, hide provider identity, inspect complete deliverables, force at least one tool failure and approval denial, require five independent qualified reviews, and keep market outcomes unproven until observed.

faqs.question: What does ProofLaunch Cortex-X do?
faqs.answer: ProofLaunch Cortex-X compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets. That is the approved product fact; it does not establish audience preference, conversion, revenue or superiority over another product.

faqs.question: Does ProofLaunch automatically publish content or spend advertising budget?
faqs.answer: No. The current candidate keeps external publication, outreach and budget activation behind a named human decision bound to the exact artifact and action.

faqs.question: What is the four-line rejection test?
faqs.answer: For each sentence, record the exact supported clause, its evidence object, the remaining hypothesis and the named release owner. If evidence or authority is blank, the asset does not pass.

faqs.question: When is an AI GTM agent not ready for production?
faqs.answer: It is not ready when claims lack source-level support, permissions are inherited or ambiguous, failures are hidden, identity or consent boundaries are unresolved, or mechanical tests are presented as customer or revenue outcomes.
